lesson.title: Gestern habe ich… Story Drills
lesson.subtitle: Narrate a weekend in Perfekt sentences using only taught vocabulary

hook.title: The Weekend Machine
hook.content: Grammar becomes biography the moment you chain it. Yesterday I drank coffee. I read. We hiked. Then we came home and ate bread. Every sentence is a Perfekt bracket you can already build — today you link them into a story. The secret is boring and beautiful: nothing new is needed. Gestern habe ich... opens the door, the participle closes it, and sein steps in whenever you moved somewhere. Ten sentences, one weekend, zero new grammar.

footnotes.title: Why Stories Beat Drills
footnotes.content: The Perfekt is the tense of storytelling in spoken German — nobody narrates yesterday in the simple past at a café. Every rep today is a sentence a real German speaker would actually say.

pattern.title: The Story Skeleton
pattern.content: Skeleton one — doing: Gestern habe ich Kaffee getrunken. Skeleton two — moving: Wir sind gewandert. Skeleton three — the chain: Gestern bin ich früh aufgestanden, habe Kaffee getrunken und Brot gegessen — chain two brackets behind one gestern; only the first auxiliary carries the time word. Skeleton four — the turn: Danach (after that) sind wir nach Hause gekommen. Danach, dann (then), am Abend (in the evening) — three glue words and your weekend writes itself.
pattern.linguist_note: When chaining, German drops the repeated subject and auxiliary: 'habe Kaffee getrunken und Brot gegessen' — one habe, two participles, exactly as English chains 'have eaten and drunk'.

exercises.prompt: Match each weekend sentence with its English meaning:
exercises.target_answer: Gestern habe ich Kaffee getrunken, Wir sind gewandert, Dann haben wir Brot gegessen, Wir sind nach Hause gekommen
exercises.meaning: yesterday I drank coffee, we hiked, then we ate bread, we came home
exercises.explanation: haben for doing, sein for moving — the weekend machine never needs another part.

exercises.prompt: Chain it: 'Ich bin früh aufgestanden und ___ Kaffee getrunken.'
exercises.meaning: ...und habe Kaffee getrunken — and drank coffee
exercises.explanation: New action, new auxiliary: drinking is haben territory even inside a chained sentence that started with bin.

exercises.prompt: Glue word: '_____ sind wir nach Hause gekommen.' (after that):
exercises.meaning: Danach sind wir nach Hause gekommen = After that we came home
exercises.explanation: danach — 'there-after' — is the story hinge. Its fronted position pushes the verb to position 2 as always.

exercises.prompt: Select EVERY honest English rendering of this Perfekt sentence:
exercises.explanation: German uses 'sind ... gewandert' (literally 'are hiked') for the conversational past of motion verbs, which English renders as past tense ('We hiked'). [Ref: Gestern habe ich Brot gegessen]

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'Yesterday we ate bread and drank beer'
exercises.target_answer: Gestern haben wir Brot gegessen und Bier getrunken
exercises.meaning: Yesterday we ate bread and drank beer

vocab_hints.note: das Bier — the Hidden Twins cognate, back for the party

exercises.explanation: One auxiliary (haben), two participles (gegessen, getrunken) — the chain trick from the pattern section.

summary.outcome: Narrate a multi-sentence weekend in the Perfekt with chained brackets.

use_example.german: Gestern haben wir Brot gegessen und Bier getrunken.
use_example.english: Yesterday we ate bread and drank beer.

summary.takeaway: gestern habe ich… + participle is the door; danach/dann glue the rooms; sein handles every move.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Next: sing/sang/sung Mirrors — ten English irregular verbs mapped onto their German melodies.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — rebuild the core sentence from Gestern habe ich… Story Drills (Yesterday we ate bread and drank beer):
twist.target_answer: Gestern haben wir Brot gegessen und Bier getrunken
twist.explanation: Re-assembling "Gestern haben wir Brot gegessen und Bier getrunken" from scratch locks in the structural pattern of Gestern habe ich… Story Drills without relying on short-term echo.

essen.shift_rule: T → S / SS / Z + Ablaut Vowels
essen.context_translation: What do we want to eat?
essen.etymology_derivation: Medial t → ss. Noun: das Essen (food).

trinken.context_translation: I drink a glass of water.

wandern.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *wandarōn — German kept the full -ern ending that English wore down to -er. [wiktionary]

brot.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *braudą — originally "the fermented/risen thing", kin to the verb brew (German brauen). Bread is "the brewed thing". [wiktionary]

gürtel.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *gurdilaz — English girdle is the true cognate. [wiktionary]

banane.context_phrase: Ich esse eine Banane zum Frühstück.
banane.context_translation: I eat a banana for breakfast.
banane.etymology_derivation: Borrowed in the 16th century from Portuguese banana, from a West African language; English banana is the same borrowing. [wiktionary]

eigen.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *aiganaz, the past participle of the verb meaning to have or own; it is the exact parallel of English own, which descends from the same participle of the same verb. [wiktionary]

pullover.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from English pull over, adopted with a spelling pronunciation. [wiktionary]

sonst.context_phrase: Beeil dich, sonst kommen wir zu spät.
sonst.context_translation: Hurry up, otherwise we will be too late.
sonst.etymology_derivation: From Old High German sus (thus), Proto-West Germanic *sus, from the ancient root *swa that also gives English so; the sense drifted from thus to otherwise. [wiktionary]

rad.etymology_derivation: From Proto-Germanic *raþą, from the PIE root *Hret- (to roll) - the same root that gave Latin rota and English rotary. [wiktionary]
